commit.message:
[HIP] [FlyDSL] feat(flydsl): row-group FP4 paged MQA logits for 8- and 64-row pages (#6145)

* feat(flydsl): row-group FP4 paged MQA logits for 8- and 64-row pages

Add pa_mqa_logits_fp4_rowgroup, an FP4 paged MQA logits kernel in which a
wave scores a group of a sequence's query rows off each key load (the
existing kernel reads every key once per row), and route
flydsl_pa_mqa_logits_fp4 to it for kv_block_size 8 and 64.

- Page 64 keeps the existing preshuffled cache layout and its writers;
  page 8 (DeepSeek-V4.1's indexer pages) has its own layout
  (pack_kv_cache), so a candidate layer's kept blocks are its block table
  with no gather.
- Work is shared out by each sequence's real length inside the kernel
  (static split, or a length-balanced share when that walks shorter); the
  grid depends on the batch and max_seq_len only, so a captured graph keeps
  it. No schedule launch; cta_info / block_k / num_warps /
  parallel_unit_num do not apply on this path.
- Keys and scales are read through 64-bit addresses (pools past 4 GiB);
  sequences are handled in runtime chunks of 64 (one build per shape for
  any batch).
- A given `out` is left as it was past each row's bound (no -inf fill).
- compute_varctx_schedule moves to pa_mqa_logits_fp4_common.

Cold, MI355X, against the original FlyDSL kernel (its schedule prebuilt):
page 64 1.07-3.0x (B = 64, H 32/64, next_n 1/2/6, up to 100K keys) and
1.25-2.9x at B = 1-16; page 8 V4.1 full layers 1.5-3.4x (T = 6-768, 200K
context). Against aiter's Triton paged_mxfp4_mqa_logits: page 8 1.03-1.5x
on every T; page 64 ahead or level on most shapes.

Also: rope_rotate_activation (fp4) gains round_rope, rounding the rotated
values to the input dtype before quantizing them, as a model whose RoPE
writes its output back in that dtype (DeepSeek-V4.1's index query) does;
with a bit-exact test (op_tests/test_dsv4_rotate_quant.py --round-rope).

* feat(flydsl): ragged query rows in the row-group FP4 MQA logits kernel

flydsl_pa_mqa_logits_fp4_rowgroup takes query_start_loc [B + 1] and
max_query_len: sequence b's rows are the flattened rows
query_start_loc[b] .. query_start_loc[b + 1] - 1, any count up to
max_query_len (0 included, as cudagraph padding has). q_fp4 is
[rows, 1, H, D / 2]; q_scale, weights, row_ends and out go by flattened
row. Without row_ends, row n of a count-row sequence sees
context - count + n + 1 keys.

A sequence's rows still share each key load, so a batch whose requests
carry different numbers of query rows no longer has to be scored one row a
sequence. Rows past a sequence's count read row 0 and get bound 0: no keys
walked, no stores. One build flag (ragged); counts and batch stay runtime
values. The rectangular [B, NEXT_N] call is unchanged.

V4.1 full layers (page 8, 200K context, T = 6..768, cold, MI355X): the
ragged call runs 1.0-2.35x faster than scoring each row as its own
sequence (T = 48: 24.8 vs 43.4 us, T = 768: 246 vs 580 us), and within
-4.5..+1.6% of the rectangular call; uniform counts give the rectangular
call's logits bit for bit.

* feat(flydsl): ragged row-group MQA logits take their lengths from row_ends

Ragged rows (query_start_loc) now require row_ends and take no
context_lens: a sequence's length, which the kernel shares its workgroups
out by, is its last row's bound, read in the kernel. A caller with per-row
bounds no longer builds a per-sequence length.

pages_per_block: a block-table entry may name that many consecutive pages
(its first page's id / pages_per_block), expanded in the kernel where the
page is used, so a caller whose pages are a multiple of the kernel's page
size (DeepSeek-V4.1: 16 pages of 8 rows a 128-row PAGE) passes its own
table as is.

flydsl_pa_mqa_logits_fp4 forwards row_ends, query_start_loc,
max_query_len and pages_per_block to the row-group kernel (page 8 / 64) and
refuses them on its other pages.

Uniform per-row bounds and pages_per_block = 1 build the same kernel as
before; op_tests/test_flydsl_pa_mqa_logits_fp4.py passes at page 64 and 8.

* feat(configs): DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP8 wo_b in the dsv4 mxscale bmm table

N=7168, K=2048 (128x128 blocks), M 1..65536: the attention output
projection at TP8, which had no row and took the heuristic kernel. Rows
tuned on gfx950 as the table's others were; errRatio <= 0.0009 against the
dequantized reference. Against the heuristic pick, same operands, cold:
1.01-1.03x at most M, 1.22x at M = 256. Only rows added.

* feat(flydsl): M-tile FP4 MQA row-group kernel with a shape-only launch plan

The row-group kernel scores MQA as a GEMM: M a sequence's query rows times
the heads, cut into tiles of whole rows (tile_m, a row's head sum stays in
its tile), N its keys. Prefill and decode are the same ragged rows
(query_start_loc, row_ends); next_n is gone from the kernel. Work is shared
out over M tiles by real length inside the kernel, so a long sequence's
tiles get more workgroups.

- make_fp4_mqa_plan / Fp4MqaPlan: the launch (tile from TILE_ROWS, rows a
  wave, warps, workgroups, depth, nontemporal loads) from the batch's shape
  alone, so a captured graph keeps it; lru_cached.
- flydsl_pa_mqa_logits_fp4_rowgroup(plan, ...) takes ragged rows only.
- Page 8 compiles a single depth-2 walk: the two walks in one kernel spilled
  40 VGPRs at 6 rows of 32 heads; one walk is as fast or faster on every
  shape measured (B=64 6 rows at 131K keys 185 -> 157 us, per-row tables
  T=3072 954 -> 838 us). Page 64 keeps both walks.
- Launch through a cached CompiledFunction (tensor_shim._run_compiled):
  host cost per call 87 -> 16 us (FlyDSL rebuilt the cache key from every
  argument on each call).
- flydsl_pa_mqa_logits_fp4: ragged rows (query_start_loc + row_ends, an
  optional plan) run the row-group kernel; a rectangular call runs the
  varctx kernel as before rowgroup existed, no silent conversion. The page-8
  op test passes its rows as ragged rows.

Prefill (V4.1 geometry) 1.9-13x faster than scoring each row as its own
sequence; decode on par with the previous row-group kernel; outputs
bit-exact against it.

* update

* style: black-format the row-group FP4 MQA kernel

commit.message:
[HIP] [OPUS] [FlyDSL] gfx950 MXFP8 e8m0 GEMM + DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 tuned configs (#5896)

* feat(flydsl): gfx950 MXFP8 e8m0 GEMM on FlyDSL + DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 configs

- New FlyDSL gfx950 MXFP8 batched GEMM (bmm_a8w8_mxscale_gfx950): scaled
  MFMA 16x16x128, async LDS DMA pipeline, 32x32 / 128x128 e8m0 blocks,
  split-K with same-XCD last-arrival reduction, B direct to registers, XCD
  tile order, non-temporal B, per-stage or preloaded scale panels, K % 64
  tail, column-major (blockscale) x_scale. Scale rows that are not whole
  dwords (e.g. 128-wide blocks at K = 384 / 768) are copied a byte per LDS
  slot with exact buffer bounds. check_bmm_config is the single legality
  source.
- Arch-neutral front door flydsl.batched_gemm_a8w8 dispatching by (arch,
  w_scale block, x_scale layout); gfx950 module with kernelName parsing,
  untuned-shape heuristic and a compiled-launcher cache (host 71 -> 21 us).
- gemm_a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle on gfx950 routes e8m0 x_scale + w_scale
  to it through the tuned table AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_A8W8_BLOCKSCALE_MXSCALE_
  BPRESHUFFLE; FP32 scales keep CK / asm. gemm_a8w8_blockscale with
  isBpreshuffled forwards native group32 operands there. The V4 wo_a
  batched GEMM uses the same kernel.
- AOT precompiles kernelId=bmm rows (both x_scale layouts for 128x128).
- Tuned gfx950 configs: DeepSeek-V4-Pro 128x128 linears (980 rows, TP1/4/8,
  1.30x vs CK/asm), DeepSeek-V4.1 group32 (1224 rows, 1.22x vs Triton),
  V4 wo_a batched (680 rows).
- Also carries the other local changes in the tree: inverse_rope_group_quant,
  opus policy / bmm tune, gfx1250 bmm wrapper, tensor_shim helpers.

* refactor(flydsl): tidy gfx950 MXFP8 bmm kernel per FlyDSL cleanup guide

- Use fx.copy instead of fx.copy_atom_call for the single-atom copies.
- Build the async-LDS DMA destination from the LDS pointer with
  fx.add_offset + fx.to_llvm_ptr instead of ptrtoint/inttoptr with a
  hand-picked address space. The raw buffer_load_async_lds stays: the
  BufferLoadAsyncLDS atom has no 1-byte size and no cache-policy operand.
- Factor the compile-and-run + leaked ir.Context recovery out of
  tensor_shim._run_compiled into _compile_and_run, and use it for the
  bmm wrapper's per-config compile cache too.

Generated ISA is byte-identical on 9 reference configs.
